verdicts.claim: C1. No shape + spelling variant gives about 1,000 root forms that are single tokens in all 7 tokenizers and have max zipf < 3; the single-token forms that pass the filter are almost all fragments of common English words.
verdicts.evidence: I rechecked inventory.json and got the same lists: CVC ␣kat all7_lt3 32, CVCC ␣kat 78, CVC kat 41, VCVC kat 225. A full enumeration of CVC ␣kat also gives 32. I then ran a check that does not depend on shape (verify/v_inventory.py): intersect the 7 vocabularies, confirm in context after 'the' that each form is one token, and apply the 11-language zipf<3 filter. That leaves 657 forms with a leading space, of any shape (450 start with a consonant). 205 of them fall in inventory.py's 8 root shapes, which matches inventory.md's 205. Leading space plus capital gives 160. Bare forms give 1,953 (492 start with a consonant), but bare forms only stay single tokens at the start of a letter run, so they do not help glued text. So with a leading space, no shape reaches 1,000 in all 7 tokenizers. Caveat 1: without mistral_sp, the shape-free leading-space pool is 1,344 (941 start with a consonant). That is above 1,000. inventory.md reports 319 for this case because it pools only 8 shapes (verify/v_inventory_nosp.out). Caveat 2, fragments: 84% of the 657 are proper prefixes of English words with zipf>=3 (89% for 11 languages). The control, random strings of the same lengths, scores 0% (2% for 11 languages). Most of the other 103 are code identifiers or technical English (argc, kwargs, json, regex, numpy, parse, retry, callback) or Spanish stems (encontr, llam). So 'almost all English fragments' is about 84%, and the remainder carries just as much meaning. (verify/pool.py and pool_attempt_1.json were already in verify/, written by another process. I did not use them.)

verdicts.claim: C2. With forms picked to be single tokens, writing every morpheme separated by spaces (W2) gives morpheme = token (about 1.01 tokens per morpheme) on 5 of 7 tokenizers; gluing (W1) misaligns (recall ~0.8, precision 0.57-0.72).
verdicts.evidence: alignment.json, token_picked W2: tokens per morpheme 1.0072-1.0125 with precision 0.987-0.993 on o200k, cl100k, llama3, llama4 and mistral_tekken. claude_legacy is 1.126 (precision 0.885) and mistral_sp 1.330 (precision 0.746). I replicated this independently (verify/v_alignment.py) with my own message generator (3-8 words per message) and my own boundary code on the same 59 roots and 34 affixes. W2 gave 1.019-1.035 tokens per morpheme with precision 0.963-0.980 on the same 5 tokenizers, so the strict criterion still passes. claude_legacy gave 1.091/0.911 and mistral_sp 1.310/0.750. W1 gave 1.09-1.22 tokens per morpheme, recall 0.765-0.825, precision 0.666-0.724. Caveats: (1) The result rests on 59 CVC roots, and the affixes were filtered at zipf<4.5. At zipf<3 the token-picked VC affix pool is empty. (2) With a realistic lexicon (150 closed-class forms plus 1,000 roots, taken from projection's ordered forms), W2 gives 1.075 (o200k), 1.077 (llama4), 1.139 (tekken), 1.224 (llama3), 1.277 (cl100k), 1.372 (claude_legacy) and 1.421 (mistral_sp) tokens per morpheme. That is 0 of 7 passing strict. In the actual projected corpus texts, with raw strings removed: o200k 1.040-1.056, llama4 1.037-1.053, tekken 1.08-1.11, llama3 1.11-1.16, cl100k 1.14-1.20, claude_legacy 1.24-1.35, mistral_sp 1.31-1.44 (verify/v_tpm_projected.out). (3) With the 205-root pool that is single-token in all 7, W2 passes strict on 7 of 7 (1.000-1.044, precision >= 0.955). So '5 of 7' comes from the 6-of-7 CVC selection rule, not from W2 itself. With the realistic lexicon, W1 is worse than claimed: recall 0.64-0.69, precision 0.40-0.43.

verdicts.claim: C3. Even at S5 (defaults elided, AGT/PAT/THM dropped, LNK/ATR dropped, raw digits), the language costs about 1.27-1.30x en_terse on o200k and 1.53-1.59x on claude_legacy (about 0.93-0.95x en on o200k).
verdicts.evidence:
I reimplemented projection.py from the gloss conventions (verify/v_projection.py). It reproduces every token total in projection.json exactly: 6 scenarios x 7 tokenizers x 2 glossers, zero differences. Recounted S0 equals the declared total_strict for every message (1480 and 1442), and S1 equals the declared total_elided for every message (1229 and 1169). The default markers removed number 251 (gloss 1) and 273 (gloss 2). The S5 digit strings match the English numerals (verify/v_numbers.out). S5 totals: o200k 1075/1105, which is 1.27/1.30x en_terse and 0.93/0.95x en; claude_legacy 1310/1359, which is 1.53/1.59x en_terse. The language uses fewer tokens than en_terse in only 1 of 40 messages on o200k and 0 of 40 on claude_legacy. The direction holds in every variant I ran (S5 vs en_terse, gloss 1/gloss 2):
- Lexicon ordered by o200k cost only: o200k 1.25/1.28.
- Lexicon ordered by claude_legacy cost only: claude_legacy 1.45/1.50.
- 300 roots instead of 1,000: o200k 1.24/1.28, claude_legacy 1.40/1.45.
- Word filter zipf<4: claude_legacy 1.29/1.33.
- No word filter at all: o200k 1.22/1.25, claude_legacy 1.20/1.23.
- Shape-free single-token pool first: o200k 1.24/1.27, claude_legacy 1.30/1.34.
So the claude_legacy magnitude depends mostly on the word filter and the 6-shape candidate list, but the direction does not. S5 already needs 21.7/22.6 morphemes per message, while en_terse costs 21.2 o200k tokens per message. S5's raw digits are an explicit relaxation of the a-z rule. The compliant S4 costs 1.29/1.33x en_terse on o200k and 1.60/1.65x on claude_legacy.

verdicts.claim: C4. Fusing speech act + confidence + evidentiality into one affix saves nothing beyond eliding defaults.
verdicts.evidence: Replicated: S2 minus S1 is 0 tokens for gloss 1 and -2 for gloss 2 on all 7 tokenizers. Fusion can only save when one clause keeps two or more non-default values. That happens in 0 of 104 clauses in gloss 1 and 2 of 121 in gloss 2. Exactly one non-default value appears in 61/104 and 86/121 clusters, and none in 43 and 33. All 225 clusters are contiguous triples with the speech act first, so realize()'s grouping is not splitting them wrongly. The null result is therefore a property of this corpus, where non-default values rarely occur together. It is not a general result. The extra spec cost of fusion (many more affix combinations to define) was not measured.

verdicts.claim: C5. Baseline: en_terse about 0.74x en; compact JSON about 1.00x; Korean about 1.65x.
verdicts.evidence: verify/v_baseline.py re-tokenized all 40 x 4 texts on the 7 tokenizers: 0 mismatches against baseline.json per_message, and the ids match the corpus. Ratios to en: en_terse 0.725-0.764 (mean 0.737); json 0.937-1.131 (mean 1.000); ko 1.162-2.293 (mean 1.648). The means hide a wide spread. ko is 1.30 on o200k but 2.21 on claude_legacy. JSON per message ranges 0.56-1.67 on o200k (median 0.95) and 0.68-1.89 on claude_legacy. Adding a leading space to the en messages changes counts only on mistral_sp (+40).

bugs.description: Form costs are measured as ' form' after 'the', and form choice relies on those costs. But render() (line 161) joins with spaces, so the first morpheme of each message has no leading space. Forms such as 'phim', 'fenn' and 'ymax' then split into 2 tokens on o200k (ph|im, f|enn, y|max).
bugs.impact_on_numbers: Biased against the language. S5 o200k is 28 tokens too high for gloss 1 (1075 vs 1047 with a leading space) and 24 for gloss 2 (1105 vs 1081). That moves the ratio to en_terse from 1.27 to 1.23 and from 1.30 to 1.27. claude_legacy changes by 0-5 tokens; mistral_sp by 0. en counts do not change with a leading space on 6 of 7 tokenizers.

bugs.description: The morpheme budget in baseline.md section 7 divides by E2's token_picked W2 tokens per morpheme (o200k 1.01, claude_legacy 1.13, mistral_sp 1.33). Those values come from a 59-root lexicon that C1 shows cannot scale to 1,000 roots.
bugs.impact_on_numbers: Overstates the budget. In the real projected texts, tokens per morpheme is 1.04-1.06 on o200k and 1.24-1.35 on claude_legacy. The claude_legacy budget to match en_terse becomes about 15.9-17.2 morphemes per message, not 19.0. C3 itself is unaffected.

bugs.description: Root pools only include 8 consonant-initial shapes (CV, CVV, CCV, CVC, CVCV, CCVC, CVCC, CVCVC). The 'pooled' counts used for the spaced design therefore miss single-token forms of other shapes (CVCCVC, CVVC, CCVCC, and so on), even though shape is free once spaces mark boundaries.
bugs.impact_on_numbers: For all 7 tokenizers the shape-free pool is 657 (zipf<3, leading space) against the 205 reported, so C1 is unchanged. Without mistral_sp it is 1,344 (941 consonant-initial) against the 319 reported, which reverses inventory.md's statement that the 1,000-root target cannot be met even without mistral_sp.

bugs.description: Latent: realize() starts a pragmatic group at any member label and ends it at the next speech-act label. If confidence or evidentiality came before the act, or another affix sat between them, S2 would produce two fused labels instead of one.
bugs.impact_on_numbers: None on the current glosses. All 225 clusters are contiguous triples with the act first, and an independent cluster definition reproduces S2 exactly.

bugs.description: VAR labels (both glossers count them as roots) are put in the closed class and get the cheapest forms.
bugs.impact_on_numbers: Negligible, and not in a consistent direction. Moving the 23 VAR uses (gloss 1) and 22 (gloss 2) into the root class changes S5 by -4/+1 tokens on o200k and +24/-18 on claude_legacy. That also shows about ±2% noise on claude_legacy from root-form assignment alone.

bugs.description: Latent SentencePiece edge cases. Input that starts with a space produces an extra '▁' piece, so pieces() no longer joins back to the input and boundaries() is shifted by one. Separately, line 55 decodes byte-fallback pieces one at a time with errors='replace', so boundaries() is wrong for non-ASCII text.
bugs.impact_on_numbers: None in the current scripts. inventory.py and projection.py measure after a 'the' context, alignment.py removes the leading space for mistral_sp, every message starts without a space, and the Korean text only goes through count(). The inventory sanity table's 405-760 disagreements between in-context and standalone results on mistral_sp come from this dummy prefix and are expected.

biases: In favor of the language: S3 and S4 drop the role, linker and modifier affixes that the glossers' own grammars need for parsing, and charge nothing for a replacement. In gloss 1, a word without a role affix is read as a predicate and ATR marks modifiers. Gloss 1 loses 263 morphemes (21% of S1) and gloss 2 loses 168 (14%), which is about the same number of o200k tokens (1357 to 1094 and 1292 to 1124).

In favor of the language: foreign strings (RAW/STR) keep their uppercase letters, digits and punctuation in every scenario, S0-S5. There are 45 strings with 606 characters, 164 of them outside a-z. They cost 76-79 o200k tokens, 5.8-7.3% of the totals. An a-z-only escape scheme would cost more; I could not measure how much because no scheme is defined.
In favor of the language: S5 writes raw digits, which breaks the a-z rule. The compliant S4 costs 1.29/1.33x en_terse on o200k and 1.60/1.65x on claude_legacy.

In favor of the language: the spec's context cost (the docs target up to 20k tokens) is never counted. It would not change any conclusion, because the language does not beat en_terse even before that cost.

In favor of the language (C2): the token-picked affixes use a looser filter, zipf<4.5, so the pool includes real short words such as ox, ow, uh and ax. At the roots' zipf<3, the token-picked VC affix pool is empty. The 59-root pool cannot scale to 1,000 roots.

Against the language: the 11-language zipf<3 filter is strict. Loosening it to zipf<4 brings claude_legacy S5 from 1.53/1.59 down to 1.29/1.33x en_terse, and no filter gives 1.20/1.23. On o200k the effect is small: 1.27/1.30, then 1.23/1.26, then 1.22/1.25.

Against the language: projection.py only draws forms from 6 consonant-initial shapes. Putting the 657 shape-free forms that are single tokens in all 7 first lowers the average root cost on claude_legacy from 1.82 to 1.34 tokens, and S5 becomes 1.30/1.34x en_terse on claude_legacy and 1.24/1.27x on o200k.
Against the language: the first morpheme of each message has no leading space, which adds 24-28 tokens on o200k across the 40 messages (about 2.5%).

Against the language: every number is written as a number marker plus one morpheme per digit, even one/two/three, which are a single token in English. Raw digits also cost an extra space token on 6 of 7 tokenizers (o200k ' 1200' splits as ' ', '120', '0'). Only claude_legacy keeps ' 1200' as one token.

Favors the competitor: the en_terse abbreviations were chosen by measuring these same tokenizers (the authors say so). en_terse sometimes drops hedges that the glosses keep (m05 'should finish' becomes 'ETA'), and the glosses were made from en rather than en_terse.

Proxy risk: claude_legacy is a Claude-2-era tokenizer, so none of the Claude-specific magnitudes (1.53-1.59x, 1.13-1.35 tokens per morpheme) may carry over to current Claude. Root-form assignment alone moves claude_legacy totals by about ±2%.
